items.description: The gang dies in a car chase, but the bank money is still out there, somewhere in a car sold to a carnival. An insurance man heads for the midway.
Half a million dollars of train payroll and a robber posing as a doctor. The insurance man on the case has to postpone his Mexico vacation. Crime ruins everyone's plans.
Eighteen years is a long time to plan a revenge. A New Mexico single mother buys a gun and tapes a message for her daughter, just in case.
Lawrence Tierney glowers his way from small time crook to Public Enemy Number One. He holds up a cinema on the way, which feels like a rude thing to do to a moviegoer.
Holmes takes a vacation and, naturally, finds a double murder, a missing racehorse and Moriarty. Arthur Wontner plays him as a man who has never relaxed in his life.
Sydney Greenstreet loses his Scotland Yard job over a wrongful execution and would love to see his smug replacement look foolish. Peter Lorre, an artist with macabre tastes, agrees.
The brass tells a lieutenant to drop a mob boss because the stakeout is too expensive. He goes to the boss's girlfriend instead. The shadows are deep enough to hide a body in.
Pushed off a cliff by his wife's lover, a businessman survives, and the police put his wife in jail over it. Being dead turns out to be oddly convenient.
A homicide lieutenant covers up a shooting for his lover, then draws the case himself. His eager kid brother is on it too. Family dinners will be awkward.

A job gets pulled clean and the plan is to sit on the money for three years, until the statute of limitations runs out. Dane Clark leads; William Talman, later Perry Mason's Hamilton Burger, is in the cast.
Dumping a political murder victim at the door of police headquarters shows either nerve or a poor sense of direction. A lieutenant has to find out which.
Metal fatigue is not what thrillers usually fight over, but here a dying professor passes the formula to a young man. Tom Conway is the suave detective who arrives unflappable.
Frank Sinatra, cast against type, takes a widow's house hostage to ambush the President passing through. A small town is about to have a very bad day.
Bored with his desk and his family, an insurance adjuster goes to recover a thief's presents from his girlfriend, and finds an affair instead. A dull job looks better in hindsight.
Stamp collecting turns out to be a murderous hobby. A wealthy American hires private eye Tom Martin to find out if his rare stamp is a fake.
Fake money, with plates engraved by a lifer inside San Quentin. A Secret Service agent poses as a big buyer to get near the gang. The danger is real.
Burt Lancaster drives armored cars for a living, which in a noir is a warning. His ex wife keeps turning up, and so does Dan Duryea.
Adapted from a Cornell Woolrich novel, so the jobless veteran who returns a wallet and lands a chauffeur's job for a man with violent enemies is already in trouble. Havana is the way out, at a price.
In his recurring dream, a young man watches his mother fall for a dangerous stranger. Then the stranger turns up, as dream strangers do. Edgar G. Ulmer directs it like a nightmare on a budget.
One explorer bets he can spend the night alone in the Chamber of Horrors. Crooks, meanwhile, are after his ward's fortune. The wax figures stay calm.
Hired as a businessman's secret bodyguard, a lawyer shoots the man who turns up with a gun. Then he begins to suspect he was hired for exactly that.
Chester Morris goes undercover with a gang that prints fake money to rescue a kidnapped Treasury engraver. He also finds time for two sisters. T men never clock out.
The plan: a crooked lawyer and a con woman pass a gambler off as a rich couple's long lost son. Edmond O'Brien is the gambler who has to sell it.
On a beach at night, a widow thinks she hears her late husband calling from the surf. A tall dark stranger conveniently knows all about such things. Turhan Bey is the stranger.
Scotland Yard is hunting a London strangler, and so is a reporter who writes thrillers on the side. She found one of the bodies and intends to sell the story twice.
Waking from a dream of murder in a mirrored room, a bank teller finds bruises he cannot explain. DeForest Kelley, long before Star Trek, is the man waking up.
The gang hiding at the lodge has a wounded leader, and the new guest says he is a doctor. He is an insurance investigator, which complicates the surgery.

Republic Pictures, one Chicago night, and a Chicago Police technical adviser in the credits so that someone is accountable. Gig Young, Mala Powers, Marie Windsor. "Two old fashions. No ice, no water, no sugar, no grenadine."
Flying to London for an old flame, an American watches the man standing next to him at the airport get shot. Scotland Yard takes an interest in Lloyd Bridges.
Cleo Moore is the waitress who steals $25,000 from the boss who cheated her father, hides it, and confesses. Hugo Haas wrote, directed and co stars, so fate and irony get plenty of screen time.
Out of a painting of a cardinal comes a voice, and it wants a card cheat to join a counterfeiting plot. Holmes blames Moriarty, which is usually the right answer.
Los Angeles motorcycle cops chase a hit and run the police think was deliberate. A trainee goes undercover as a car thief to get close. Traffic duty has never been so exciting.
Boris Karloff takes a break from monsters to play San Francisco detective James Lee Wong. A friend of the police captain is murdered and the trail runs along the waterfront.
Stop in the rain to help a stranded motorist and you wake up with the truck gone. A driver with a record is the police's first suspect. Never stop for a stranger.
Temporarily blind, a man wanders into a house just after a murder. The killers spare him, the police do not believe him, and nobody can find a body.
One kiss between a bookstore manager and a clerk, and the thief she is dating smells blackmail. Hammer made it before it found its monsters, with Terence Fisher directing.
A childhood secret that the town has built a career on. Stanwyck and Heflin walk back into it, and a very young Kirk Douglas is already sweating.
Joan Crawford is a playwright who turns down an actor for looking wrong and then falls for him on a train. Jack Palance's eyebrows carry the suspense.
After a robbery goes sour, a wounded rebel leader drifts through the back alleys of Belfast with the whole city hunting him. Carol Reed directs James Mason through all of it.
Every hitchhiking warning you were ever given, in one car. A killer fresh from a holdup catches a ride to Los Angeles, picks up passengers and takes charge.
Glenn Ford comes home from Korea to his train and a rail supervisor's wife. Fritz Lang directs, and Gloria Grahame is the reason the engineer is in trouble.
Ingrid Bergman, a psychiatrist, falls for the asylum's new director, who has some very odd aversions. Salvador Dali designed the dream, for Alfred Hitchcock.
James Mason is a neurosurgeon lecturing students on a woman who fell from a window, and why he decided it was murder. He skips the police and handles it himself.
Anatole Litvak remakes Marcel Carné's Le jour se lève for RKO, with Henry Fonda in Jean Gabin's old part and Vincent Price permitted a bow tie. Most of it is spent at night.
Tony Curtis goes to Macao to fetch an old flame for a mobster, and she turns out to be engaged to the casino owner he just saved. Rescuing people is a poor career move.
PRC Pictures, Lew Landers directing, a lot of desert. A man cannot remember who he is, and a ranch house fills with people who might know. "Jim, you mustn't dwell on yourself so intensely."
A veteran comes home to find his gangster brother dead and takes over the rackets in the name of revenge. His sweetheart would prefer he quit. Family business, though.
A pianist hitchhikes to Los Angeles, his ride dies on a rainy night, and he makes the worst decision available. Ann Savage then arrives as the meanest woman in noir.
A poisoned dart, a dying woman and a half written clue, all in detective James Lee Wong's front hall. Boris Karloff has fog, a waterfront and two suspects who start with J.
A smash and grab crook with broken wrists does his time without naming the club owner who ran out on him. William Hartnell, the first Doctor Who, spends the sentence building a grudge.
Women marry soldiers for their pay and their life insurance, and would like the soldiers not to come home. Kay Francis is in the middle of the racket. A wartime scam with excellent hats.
Masked men rob an armored car, and an ex GI takes the beating from the police. John Payne follows the trail to Mexico to find who set him up.
A mild cashier and amateur painter rescues a woman from a beating, and she lets him think she loves him. Edward G. Robinson, Joan Bennett and Dan Duryea make a bad triangle.
The Shadow catches safecrackers, then fools the police by pretending to be the lawyer whose safe it was. Rod La Rocque plays the hero of the pulps and radio, in a very good hat.
Barbara Stanwyck is a famous advice columnist who gives it all up to marry a detective. She turns out to be very ambitious on his behalf.
A week's fun in San Francisco turns into a luminous poison and no antidote. A small town accountant spends what is left investigating his own murder.
